sara (ml-eng): Heads-up — we're trying to bring Vellichor-7B into the catalog. License is a bit unusual, asking for attribution metadata and has a dual-license clause for commercial users. Also want to confirm whether we can ship quantized weights to Dedicated customers. :eyes:
sam (legal): Can you paste the exact license text or a link? dual-license can mean a bunch of things. :thinking:
sara (ml-eng): Here's the header — the repo has a short LICENSE file.
```
Vellichor Research License v1.0
- Noncommercial: free for research & academic use
- Commercial: requires separate commercial license or opt-in dual-license A/B (see appendix)
- Attribution required in product UI and in model card
- Redistributing modified model (including quantized/converted weights) requires notice to authors
```
ryan (ml-eng): Quick context: our quantization pipeline produces a .q4_0-weight file and we generally package models in a container image for Dedicated. Is that "redistributing modified model"?
sam (legal): Short answer: probably yes. Quantized weights are usually considered a derivative. The attribution + notification clause is enforceable if it's clear in the license. Need to see the appendix for the commercial path.
liz (product): If customers are charged usage fees on Hosted or Dedicated, does that trigger the commercial requirement automatically? We need a clear policy before we add it to the hosted catalog.
sam (legal): If the license ties "commercial use" to charging money for access, then offering it in a paid Dedicated contract likely triggers the commercial license. Self-serve free credits for evaluation might be okay under noncommercial, but it's ambiguous. Recommend we ask upstream for clarification or get a commercial license.
sara (ml-eng): For Dedicated onboarding we also have contractual obligations around customer-controlled artifacts. Toni — from ops side, is shipping quantized weights inside Dedicated container standard?
toni (ops): Yes, we ship model artifacts in images for Dedicated. If licensing requires a notice, we can add a model card file at /model-card/NOTICE.txt inside the image and surface attribution in the console. But legal needs to confirm that's sufficient.
sam (legal): Attribution in UI + model card file is a reasonable mitigation. But the redistribution notice clause — "requires notice to authors" — could imply we need explicit permission before packaging for Dedicated customers. If that's the case, passive attribution won't satisfy the redistribution restriction.
ryan (ml-eng): Practical ask: if we add a clear model-card with author attribution and a checkbox during deployment that we contacted authors (or that we've purchased a commercial license), is that an acceptable operational flow?
sam (legal): Two options: 1) get a written commercial license from the upstream that permits redistribution of quantized derivatives (cleanest), or 2) restrict onboarding to Hosted eval-only and Private (customer brings their own weights) until we get written permission. The checkbox alone is risky.
liz (product): Timeline impact? Sales wants this in Dedicated catalog next quarter for an enterprise lead. If legal needs a signed license, how long might that take?
sam (legal): Could be days to weeks depending on upstream responsiveness and their legal team. I'll ping them today. If they accept a standard commercial addendum, we can fast-track.
sara (ml-eng): Notes about technical constraints: quantizing Vellichor-7B to q4_0 yields ~2.5x speedups with minor perplexity delta on our evals. We already ran the internal regression suite — small drop for long-context summarization tests. I can include eval output.
ryan (ml-eng): Attaching short eval summary (pasted):
```
- Summarization (long): +3.2% rouge drop at q4_0
- Chat turn latency: -48% median tokens/sec improvement
- Safety evals: no new hallucination patterns found in our small prompt set
```
sam (legal): Good to have. Please also capture provenance of training data if available; some licenses restrict downstream usage depending on training data sources.
sara (ml-eng): Upstream model card mentions mixed proprietary crawls and CC data — nothing flagged as restricted but not super detailed. I'll add a note asking them for provenance details.
toni (ops): Ops question: if we get permission to redistribute quantized weights, do we need to lock them behind dedicated agreements (no public hosting)? Any redlines we should expect?
sam (legal): Likely yes. Upstream might allow redistribution only to customers who have signed a downstream license or via a controlled distribution channel. We should be prepared for: per-customer attribution, restrictions on public model zoo, and reporting obligations.
liz (product): For product messaging, we should avoid implying "open" if we're operating under a paid redistrib model. Let's draft two catalog variants: "Eval in Hosted (noncommercial)" and "Enterprise Dedicated with commercial license" so customers see the difference.
sara (ml-eng): Will follow up with an eval bundle + the exact LICENSE appendix link. Also flagging that model family name "Vellichor" needs an explicit trademark check.
sam (legal): Copy that. I'll reach out to upstream and loop in security for provenance checks. If they sign a permissive commercial addendum, we can proceed with packaging quantized weights into Dedicated images and add the model card + console attribution. Otherwise we keep it eval-only or Private BYO-weights.
deploy-bot: Deployment notice — sandbox image build completed for vellichor-7b-q4_0 at sha: f2a9c3b (for internal eval only). :rocket:
sara (ml-eng): Thanks — I'll attach the eval artifacts in the ticket and tag this thread when we have upstream reply. :thumbsup:
